description: A thoughtfully layered living room corner photographed at seated eye-level with a normal lens, framed as a close three-quarter view showing the side table and adjacent wall. The walls are clad in white-painted brick, adding a raw, textural quality to the otherwise polished space. On the left edge, a chunky charcoal grey sofa is partially visible with a loosely draped cream knit throw. A sculptural live-edge or organic-form wood coffee or side table in warm walnut with an irregular, organic top sits at center, holding a small dark ceramic bowl and a tight cluster of books. Beside it, a slim glass vase with a single dried branch adds a delicate vertical line. A compact open shelf unit in the background holds a few books, a small white ceramic vessel, and a petite potted fiddle-leaf fig. A large-format framed artwork in bold black-and-white graphic form — abstract organic shapes — hangs on the brick wall above the shelf. A warm, upward-diffusing glow radiates from the translucent disc-form sitting on the dark cylindrical base at the table surface, spreading a broad warm pool of light across the table objects and onto the brick wall immediately behind at table height — the light does not extend to the ceiling. The palette is tonal and design-forward: white-painted brick, dark matte black, warm walnut, charcoal grey, and alabaster cream.
